evidence.source_sentence: To verify there is no homopolymerization for St, the DSC curves were recorded. characterizations.result_summary: Observed impact fracture surface micromorphology of PVC/ABS composites with different ABS content, identified brittle-ductile transition characteristics at 10 phr ABS addition.

evidence.source_sentence: The field emission SEM was used to explore the micromorphology of the impact fracture surface. As displayed in Figure  4a, the impact section of the composite material presents relatively flat with the addition of 6 phr ABS. The impact section of the PVC/ABS composite material contains well-distributed voids when the ABS is increased to 10 phr (Figure 4c). Some tree-root-like yielding fibers appear, which is a typical characteristic of toughness fracture. The fracture surface is not uniform at 12 phr (Figure 4d). Both the matrix yielding caused by the obvious plastic deformation and a number of voids, and some of the more flat and smooth planes appear the characteristics of brittle fracture.

characterizations.result_summary: Observed impact fracture surface micromorphology of PVC/ABS/SMIA composites, found no obvious phase separation, and morphology changes correlated with SMIA content and impact strength.

evidence.source_sentence: To deeply understand the impact performance of PVC/ABS/ SMIA composites, SEM images were acquired. As shown in Figure $^ { 6 , }$the boundary between the two phases was not found, and no obvious phase separation occurred. The gradual decrease in the number of yielding fibers on the surface can be observed when the SMIA content is increased from 0 to 10 phr. As the SMIA content further increases, the degree of slatting increases, the surface becomes relatively smooth, and the number of micropores gradually decreases.
